evidence: Plaut. Mil. 596: Cohibēte intrā līmen etiam vōs parumper
terms.comment: Within a boundary, at rest or going in: intrā parietēs, within one’s walls; intrā portam penetrāre pedem, to set foot inside the gate. Classically only a preposition (Lewis & Short); the adverb is intus. For “within” a time, see within (a time).
Where a thing is: inside, at home. For going in, intrō (see into).

phrases.latin: Cohibēte intrā līmen etiam vōs parumper, Pleusiclēs
phrases.english: You stay inside the door a little longer too, Pleusicles

phrases.latin: neque hūc umquam, postquam nātus sum, intrā portam penetrāvī pedem
phrases.english: and never since I was born have I set foot inside the gate here

phrases.latin: quod facile fuisset nisi intrā parietēs meōs dē meā perniciē cōnsilia inīrentur
phrases.english: which would have been easy, had plots for my ruin not been laid within my own walls

phrases.latin: sed estne frāter intus? — Nōn est.
phrases.english: But is my brother indoors? — He isn’t.

phrases.latin: fīcī enim sēmen nātūrāle intus in eā fīcō, quam edimus, quae sunt minūta grāna
phrases.english: for the fig’s natural seed is inside the fig we eat: those are the tiny grains
